context:
Planning basis: the aggressive comment/docstring-removal plan revised after external Claude Opus 5.5, medium-effort review (all 18 findings have durable dispositions in quality/comment-cleanup-scope.json). Original source baseline 0697891d449b1e31f22e4842169f3b2e743337fb. Refresh all facts at implementation start.

Plan v2 amendment (2026-10-02, decision D4, approved by the user): this item alone held 854 files and about 25,800 comments and docstrings, 27% of all Python items. It is now an umbrella that owns no work of its own: the three child items comment-cleanup-unit-tests-core, comment-cleanup-unit-tests-platforms and comment-cleanup-unit-tests-cli-scripts-rest each carry a third of the scope, and this item is done when all three are done. Its description above is the shared contract the children copy. The scope policy rules in quality/comment-cleanup-scope.json are updated in the scope-completion step so that each residual tests/unit file has exactly one of the three children as its owner; until then the rule `cross-module-unit-tests-tree` still names this item.
description:
Exclusive candidate scope: Exact tests/unit/** files not already assigned to a production/consumer/support task, frozen individually; excludes all other test manifests; matching tests/generators/outputs/reference pages only as frozen by scope-policy. Exclude other task manifests, shared integrator files, upstream/external mirrors and historical evidence. Unknown ownership/consumer blocks deletion; never expand a worker scope unilaterally.

Target: zero discretionary explanatory comments and authored explanatory docstrings in maintained first-party code. Only proven minimum machine directives and unavoidable provenance-bound required notices remain. Useful product strings must have an actual consumer; no inert constants, unused strings, fake metadata or dynamic __doc__ replacements. Never broaden lint/type/coverage ignores, weaken assertions, or turn unknown ownership/parser coverage into an exclusion.

Required work and decisions: No blanket residual directory permission. Inventory every unit test and hand module tests to its source owner first; split remaining cross-module files by existing subsystem and pilot budget before dispatch. Replace prose-source assertions with meaningful behavior/advertised metadata cases; preserve rejected cases and nonempty coverage. Unknown source readers block deletion.

Trace substantive explanation to requirement, callers, actual behavior and existing tests. Delete filler/false claims; move necessary contracts/rationale to owning external references or actually consumed metadata before deleting source text. Evaluate the smallest adequate mechanism; executable simplification/type/behavior changes require separate approval and reviewed slices, with no new abstraction solely to house prose. Preserve runtime/output consumers before removal.

Deliver source-only deletion and, where relevant, later dedicated SQL/output payload batches with explicit identity/correctness evidence. One ownership task may need multiple pilot-budget-approved PRs. Shared documentation must be published by its owner before affected deletion. Execution guard: creation of this TODO is planning, not approval to execute the reviewed cleanup. Obtain later implementation authorization. Use a separate linked worktree and agent-write-preflight; preserve unrelated work. Freeze nonoverlapping code/test/doc paths with the integrator before dispatch. Ordinary independent PRs target develop; serialize shared test-lock checks and integration, not module edits. Required native/external soundness review remains mandatory, with no auto-merge bypass. No live cloud/stress, deployment, publication, historical-result rewriting, or unapproved external-repository writes.
